decisive_items: segmental erythema and ulceration in the descending and sigmoid colon
mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon with adjacent inflammatory stranding
subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, mild crypt architectural distortion, and an acute inflammatory infiltrate without granulomas or dysplasia
response.rationale: Young-on-contraceptive patient with left-sided segmental colonic involvement, rectal sparing, bloody diarrhea, and biopsy showing edema/hemorrhage favors ischemic colitis over IBD; infectious and diverticular diagnoses are excluded by negative cultures and absence of diverticulosis.

rejected.why: Stool cultures and C. difficile assays were negative, making infectious colitis less likely.
IBD is too nonspecific; the segmental left-colonic pattern and hemorrhage favor a specific ischemic mechanism.
Normal rectal mucosa and noncontinuous involvement go against ulcerative colitis.
No granulomas and prominent edema/hemorrhage favor ischemia over Crohn's disease.
Microscopic colitis typically has nonbloody diarrhea and minimal endoscopic ulceration, not segmental hemorrhagic colitis.
CT showed no evidence of diverticulosis, perforation, or abscess.
